| [CASE-207](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-207.md) | The square twist: a crease pattern with no rigid folding motion folds once facet bending is paid for, so which configurations are connected depends on the energy available | Filed at the owner's request on 2026-11-05, to file "one or more CASEs for origami as a toy model of a resource bounded constraint configuration space". Silverberg et al. 2015 ([NOTE-1554](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1554.md)): the square twist's crease pattern is isostatic, and rigidly it has only two isolated states, unfolded and folded, yet it folds by bending its facets, a hidden degree of freedom with its own energy scale. The authors' thesis is that the number of degrees of freedom changes with the energy scale probed; their kinematic skeleton, with bending capped at 10°, has a critical plane angle near 23° separating a connected configuration space from a disconnected one. Read as a resource model, the configuration space is indexed by the budget rather than fixed, and widening the admissible moves is itself priced, which joins the vertex under a budget ([CASE-206](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-206.md)) to the curved vertex whose moves no budget widens ([CASE-204](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-204.md)). A mechanical study; its organizational reading is an analogy. Adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-208](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-208.md) | A prestressed Kresling stack: reordering the cells' energy barriers from outside opens the 8 of 56 transitions between stable states that the barrier order blocked, while the 16 that pass through other stable states are not made direct | Filed at the owner's request on 2026-11-05, to file "one or more CASEs for origami as a toy model of a resource bounded constraint configuration space". Zang, Zhao, Misseroni and Paulino ([NOTE-1569](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1569.md)): a stack of three bistable Kresling cells has 8 stable states and 56 ordered transitions; 32 are feasible, 16 cannot be made without passing through other stable states, and 8 are blocked by the order of the cells' energy barriers. Springs and handles, applied from outside, prestress the cells and reorder the barriers in place, which makes the 8 blocked transitions feasible; the 16 are not opened. Jules et al. ([NOTE-1617](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1617.md)) show the same dependence on the order of thresholds in a Kresling memory. A mechanical study; its organizational reading is an analogy. Adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
